summary: Kickoff to align on Pearl Ventures' onboarding and private deployment playbook. Reviewed network/VPC needs, security/compliance checklist (SOC2/KMS), and the first-week runbook for a staging pilot. Agreed on specific deliverables and dates; Redwood to provide playbook draft and a short latency benchmark plan.
transcript:
00:00:03 Jordan: Okay, uh, welcome everyone. This is Jordan from Redwood. Thanks for joining — we'll keep this tight, about 45 minutes. Priya and I will walk through the deployment playbook and then surface any gaps for Pearl.
00:00:12 Alicia: Great thanks Jordan. Appreciate it. We've got Marco, Devon and Samir on the line. We're mainly focused on a private VPC deployment, some on-prem constraints, and making sure we hit our security checklist.
00:00:26 Priya: Awesome. Quick intro from me — I'm Priya, SE on the onboarding team. I do infra and performance stuff. We'll start with high-level goals, then network, then security, then the pilot runbook.
00:00:38 Marco: Quick note — we use Terraform for infra and prefer not to open more than minimal egress.
00:00:44 Jordan: Noted. Okay first slide — goals. (link shared: https://redwood.example/playbooks/pv-kickoff) We want staging pilot in 2 weeks, production rollout in 8 weeks assuming the pilot passes. Success = latency <200ms p95 for common paths and <5% request error rate over 24h.
00:01:02 Samir: That p95 number — is that for the hosted API or private deploy?
00:01:05 Priya: For private deployment on your Dedicated pool; it's a target we think is achievable, but depends on model size and batching. We'll propose config in the playbook.
00:01:14 Devon: On security — we need KMS with customer-managed keys, retention controls, and audit logs. SOC2 evidence is required.
00:01:21 Jordan: Yep, we support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include the exact KMS flow in the doc. Also, we can surface audit log examples.
00:01:29 Alicia: Are there any items that require on-prem hardware? We plan to keep data in our cloud region but want to ensure no tokenized data leaves our VPC.
00:01:37 Priya: With Private deployments you can opt for a private control plane and all inference in your VPC. We'll outline the networking options: VPC peering, PrivateLink, and a tunnel-based option for air-gapped connectivity.
00:01:50 Marco: We prefer peering. We'll share CIDR ranges.
00:01:54 Jordan: Great. Moving on — network specifics. Priya?
00:01:58 Priya: Right. For peering we ask for inbound ports X, Y, and for egress minimal to Redwood endpoints. We have a diagram in the doc but to call out: KV cache traffic and model shard fetches are over the same link; if bandwidth is constrained you may see latency spikes at token peaks.
00:02:15 Marco: When you say KV cache, you mean the model's key-value cache?
00:02:18 Priya: Yeah, sorry K V cache — the attention cache. It's chatty during long contexts. We'll include a recommended MTU and keepalive settings.
00:02:26 Devon: Do you do customer-side encryption of cache?
00:02:29 Priya: Typically cache is ephemeral in RAM on the inference nodes, not persisted. But we can discuss encrypting any persisted artifacts if needed.
00:02:36 Alicia: For compliance we need proof of no PII retention. Is there a standard cert or report?
00:02:42 Jordan: We can provide retention policies and sample logs. For SOC2 we have the attestation doc — I'll attach. Also note: our private offering supports configurable retention windows.
00:02:53 Devon: And SSO — we use SAML/Okta. Need RBAC mapping with least privilege.
00:03:00 Priya: We integrate with SAML and can map roles; runbook will include role templates for 'admin', 'operator', 'auditor'.
00:03:08 Samir: On the pilot — what's the recommended workload to validate both latency and correctness?
00:03:12 Priya: We usually run a mixed load: 70% short prompts (1–2 tokens per second), 30% long chat sessions to exercise KV cache. We'll provide a bench script.
00:03:23 Jordan: I'll note that in the action items. We'll also propose quantization and batching settings in the Optimize section — note that heavier batching reduces cost but can bump p95.
00:03:33 Marco: Any threading or CPU tuning required for the inference nodes?
00:03:36 Priya: We recommend isolating GPU pods and not overcommitting CPU; sample YAML will be in the repo. Also kernel selection — oh sorry, people see weird wording sometimes, but Redwood's runtime picks kernels per model and we expose the profile.
00:03:51 Alicia: You mentioned a repo — is that a Redwood repo or a customer cloned repo?
00:03:55 Jordan: We'll share a template repo (link) with Terraform modules and Helm charts that you can copy into your infra repo.
00:04:02 Samir: Nice. On costs — is there an estimate for the Dedicated pool for our expected qps of ~20 req/s?
00:04:09 Priya: We'll include a sizing estimate in the playbook. Rough ballpark: for that QPS with mid-sized models, likely a small Dedicated pool; final number depends on model selection and sequence lengths. We can run a short benchmark to firm that up.
00:04:22 Marco: We'll need that before budget approvals.
00:04:25 Jordan: Understood. Next — security deep-dive. Devon, any specifics we should call out now?
00:04:30 Devon: Key things: KMS integration (BYOK preferred), encryption in-transit and at-rest, audit logs retention of 12 months, and SOC2 evidence. Also the ability to disable third-party telemetry.
00:04:41 Priya: All supported. We'll include steps to enable BYOK and how key rotation works. For telemetry, we have toggles for metrics collection; logs can be forwarded to your S3 or SIEM.
00:04:52 Devon: For log forwarding, format and sample schema would be helpful.
00:04:55 Priya: We'll attach sample log formats.
00:04:58 Jordan: Quick pause — any hard blockers that would prevent a 2-week staging rollout?
00:05:02 Alicia: Only the VPC peering approval timeline; selecting a model and sign-off on SOC docs are dependent on our compliance team.
00:05:09 Jordan: Okay so action: Pearl to confirm peering window and provide approvers.
00:05:14 Marco: We'll aim to send CIDRs by Monday.
00:05:18 Jordan: Great. Now the runbook: Day 0–2 provisioning, Day 3 smoke tests, Day 5 pilot open to limited traffic, Day 10 full staging soak. Priya will own the smoke test checklist.
00:05:31 Priya: Checklist highlights: infra up, model loaded, KV cache warmed, canary inference, perf baseline collected, e2e auth and SSO validated. We'll include run commands.
00:05:42 Samir: Who runs the canary? Is it Redwood or Pearl?
00:05:45 Priya: Ideally joint — we'll run the initial canary and share logs; then handoff to your ops to run repeat.
00:05:51 Devon: About telemetry — what level of detail is available without exposing raw prompts?
00:05:56 Priya: We offer token-level metrics aggregated by route and model; raw prompts can be redacted or hashed. We'll show the console filters.
00:06:06 Jordan: We also wanted to call out fallbacks — if a model variant is unavailable we can route to smaller model automatically — important for resilience during rollout.
00:06:15 Alicia: Good to know. Any manual steps for rollback?
00:06:18 Priya: Rollbacks are via the release API; for private deploys we provide a canary-to-primary flip. We'll add the command examples.
00:06:26 Jordan: Okay, questions?
00:06:29 Marco: On the peering side — what's the expected egress to Redwood? If we limit egress aggressively, will model sharding cause issues?
00:06:36 Priya: The client-side egress is mostly for model fetches and control plane calls. If you completely block egress, you break auto-updates; but we support a 'static model bundle' option for air-gapped installs. That increases ops overhead.
00:06:48 Marco: Noted. We'll evaluate.
00:06:50 Samir: Anything we should prepare for performance anomalies during the first 48h?
00:06:54 Priya: Expect higher p95 on warmup because KV cache cold-starts. Warmup scripts in the playbook help. Also, watch for tail-latency during peak concurrent long chats.
00:07:04 Devon: One more on encryption — do you support HSM attestation?
00:07:07 Jordan: We can integrate with HSM-backed KMS; we'll document supported providers.
00:07:12 Alicia: Okay great. Let's recap action items and owners.
00:07:16 Jordan: I'll read them out: Jordan to share playbook draft and SOC2 attestation; Priya to schedule infra diagram review with Marco; Marco to provide CIDRs and firewall rules; Devon to send KMS/retention questions. Does that match?
00:07:27 Marco: Yes.
00:07:28 Devon: Yes.
00:07:29 Samir: Yes.
00:07:30 Jordan: Any final topics?
00:07:32 Alicia: One ask — can Redwood provide a short, simple cost estimate slide for our finance approvers?
00:07:38 Priya: Yes, we'll include a one-pager with estimated monthly ops costs and expected run rates.
00:07:43 Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites: playbook review on 2026-11-24 and a bench-run on 2026-11-27.
00:07:52 Alicia: Thanks everyone.
00:07:54 Jordan: Thanks, we'll send notes and links. Bye.
00:08:00 [call ends early here in transcript dump — remainder of the 46 min includes small side discussions and a quick screen share walkthrough; transcript truncates but metadata records full duration]
